full_judgment:
2. The respondent No.1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 17 of 1992 in the 2nd Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Louhojong, Munshigonj for declaration of title in respect of the suit land stating, inter-alia, that the suit property originally belonged to Gafur Hawlader and Jisan Hawlader in equal 8 annas share and C.S. Khatian was correctly recorded in their names and that Jisan Hawlader died unmarried leaving his brother Gafur Hawlader who thus became 16 annas owner of the suit land and Gafur Hawlader died leaving two sons namely Sobhan  Hawlader and Alimuddin Hawlader and that Sobhan Hawlader died leaving 5 sons who are the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 5 and Alimuddin Hawlader died leaving one daughter and a widow who are the plaintiff Nos. 6 and 7 and that the plaintiffs are enjoining (enjoying) the suit property for more than 17 to 18 years through their predecessors-in-interest. But the S.A. Khatian has been prepared in the name of some other persons; that while the plaintiffs went to pay the revenue the Tahshilder refused to accept the same on the plea that the S.A. and R.S. Khatians have been recorded in the names of the defendants and that the defendants in fact had no title whatsoever nor any possession in the suit land and as a result of wrong recording of the name of the defendants in khatian, having created cloud, the plaintiff felt constrained to file the suit. 

 3. The petitioner as defendant contested the suit filing written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint. It has been stated by the defendant that one Radha Krisna was owner of the Taluk and Sasanka, Anukool and Kala Chand were the superior landlords and that C.S. record was accordingly prepared and that Gahur Hawlader and Jisan Hawlader, the predecessors of the plaintiffs, were bargaders and that their names were recorded in C.S. Khatian accordingly. It was further stated that Jisan Hawlader died unmarried and Gahur Hawlader surrendered the possession of the suit land to the superior land-lords and that Shashanka Mohan and others by an unregistered Amaldari dated 24 Agrahayon 1356 settled the suit land in favour of Prafulla and so the S.A. Khatian was recorded correctly in his name and that aforesaid Prafulla received Tk. 3600/- as advance out of Tk. 4000/-, fixed as consideration for the suit property and executed a bainapatra accordingly on 02.09.1963 in favour of the defendant and delivered possession to him and that the defendant got his name recorded in mutation case and R.S. Khatian stands recorded correctly in his name and that the plaintiff nor their predecessor had ever enjoyed the suit property and that taking advantage of the recording of names of Gahur Hawlader and Jisan Hawlader in the C.S. Khatian the plaintiffs are claiming title to the suit land illegally and hence the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 12. The basis of the claim of the defendant is S.A. Khatian but recording of the name in S.A. Khatian does not ifsofacto presume title unless the basis of the recording is proved. In order to prove the case of the plaintiff the plea of having amaldari was raised which the trial court in consideration of the evidence disbelieved, the said document being neither registered nor duly stamped and that the amaldari being disbelieved the root of the basis of the defendant falls through. The defendant-petitioner also based his claim on a bainapatra allegedly executed by Prafulla Kumar Sarker. The said bainapatra besides being unregistered was also not found to be a genuine document by the trial court which was written on a white paper and in any view of the matter a bainapatra ifsofacto does not confer title. It is surprising to find that the aforesaid bainanama marked as exhibit "Ga" was taken away by the defendant after judgment of the lower appellate court on condition of producing the same when called upon but inspite of repeated directions the defendant did not produce the said document. The High Court Division in consideration of the evidence on record endorsed the view taken by the trial court that the said document i.e. the bainapatra was also not a genuine document. If the amaldari and the bainapatra are excluded what remains for the defendant to claim the suit property? 

 13. It appears that on the basis of the aforesaid amaldari and bainapatra which have been found by the trial court as fabricated documents, the same view echoed by the High Court Division, the recording of the name of the defendant in the S.A. Khatian on the basis of the aforesaid fraudulent documents becomes unfounded and therefore the defendant's claim has no leg to stand.
